name: Upper blepharoplasty

lead: Upper blepharoplasty trims loose skin, muscle and sometimes fat from the upper eyelids through an incision hidden in the natural crease. It is done both to clear skin that blocks vision and to reduce a hooded or tired look.
The literature is mostly technique reports and case series, with a few randomised comparisons and an evidence-based review.

paras: Redundant tissue is excised along a marked ellipse in the lid crease, and the incision is closed with sutures or tissue glue. It may be paired with brow lifting or ptosis repair [5][7].

Swelling and bruising are common for several weeks [3]. Surgeons screen for dry eye, thyroid eye disease, bleeding disorders and body dysmorphic disorder beforehand [4]. Registered studies are examining dry eye and vision changes after the operation [11][12].

lead: Upper blepharoplasty is surgery on the upper eyelids that removes or repositions excess skin, orbicularis oculi muscle and sometimes fat [1][2][3]. The incision is placed in the natural eyelid crease so that the scar is concealed [3]. It is performed for functional reasons, such as excess skin (dermatochalasis) obstructing the upper visual field, and for cosmetic reasons, such as hooded or tired-looking lids [3][4].

The procedure is often combined with brow lifting or ptosis repair [5][6]. Published research includes surgical technique papers, randomised comparisons of wound closure methods [7], a 2014 evidence-based review [8], and a study of how rejuvenation surgery affects how attractive, feminine and approachable faces are perceived [9]. A number of registered trials are studying outcomes such as dry eye, vision quality and patient-reported satisfaction [10][11][12].

paras: Functional indications include dermatochalasis that impairs peripheral vision and is documented by visual field testing, which supports insurance coverage in some systems [4]. Cosmetic indications include hooded lids, fat prolapse and asymmetry, aimed at a more rested or youthful appearance [4]. Contributions from brow ptosis are sometimes addressed at the same time, since patients can compensate by overworking the frontalis muscle [4].

A skin ellipse is marked and removed along the crease, with orbicularis muscle and herniated fat removed or preserved depending on the surgeon's plan [1][4]. Reviews describe a shift from traditional excision-only approaches toward more conservative, volume-preserving and rejuvenative approaches that consider the brow and the wider periorbita [2]. Techniques reported include simultaneous brow elevation by transcoronal, limited-incision forehead or subperiosteal routes [5][6][13], and resection of the corrugator and procerus muscles through the lid incision [14]. Wound closure with octyl-2-cyanoacrylate tissue glue was compared with sutures in a randomised, blinded study of 20 patients [7].

Eyelid crease shape and fat distribution differ between populations; many people of East Asian descent have a lower crease or none, and surgery in this group is often aimed at creating a crease rather than only removing skin [3][4]. See the separate entry on non-incisional double eyelid suture.

Recovery is reported to involve swelling and bruising that generally resolve over several weeks [3]. Preoperative assessment typically screens for dry eye, thyroid eye disease and bleeding disorders, and for body dysmorphic disorder [4]. Registered studies are examining dry eye and vision quality after upper blepharoplasty [10][11][12].

A prospective, randomised, blinded study of 20 patients compared tissue glue with sutures for upper blepharoplasty closure [7]. A 2014 evidence-based medicine review summarised the literature on blepharoplasty [8]. A 2015 study examined perceived attractiveness, femininity and personality after facial rejuvenation surgery [9]. Registered trials include studies of vision quality [11], muscle versus fat removal and dry eye [12], and patient-reported outcomes with the FACE-Q instrument [10].

timeline.event: Karl Ferdinand von Gräfe coins the term 'blepharoplasty' [3].
Transcoronal brow lift with concomitant upper blepharoplasty described [5].
Randomised study of octyl-cyanoacrylate glue versus sutures in blepharoplasty [7].
Evidence-based medicine review of blepharoplasty published [8].
